newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up on local fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up on local fund buying.

text.p: Thai stocks, which were down all day, closed up 1.24 percent in moderate trade after local mutual funds entered the market late and bought blue-chip bank and finance issues, brokers said.

The SET index, which plummeted to an intraday low at 919.52 points, finished up 11.71 points at 956.34. The closing level was still the lowest in over three years. On August 25 1993 the index ended at 952.33.
"Some local mutual funds bought stocks after the finance minister Bodi asked them to buy stocks in order to help the market," said Kasem Prunratanamala of James Capel Asia.

Thai Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda said before the market closed that he would ask local mutual funds and market rescue funds operated by the government and private sector to shore up the battered local stock market.

On Monday the index fell 6.0 percent aided by foreign sales of mainly banks. Brokers said Bodi was apparently concerned about the market after the steep fall and held a meeting with other officials to discuss ways to ease the situation. Foreigners unloaded stocks on concern over corporate third quarter earnings and an expected fall in banks profit growth in 1995 from last year's 15.6 percent.
Most major sectors on the board rose today with the finance sector gained most, rising 3.76 percent. The communication sector gained 1.68 percent and the banking sector advanced 1.03 percent.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, falling one baht to 145. Finance One rose 1.50 to 85 and Advanced Info Service rose 30 to 334. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
